title: AZ-1 (Scottsdale, north Phoenix)
why_it_matters: Schweikert left to run for governor. Biden-Harris-competitive suburban seat that Democrats narrowly missed in 2024.
notes: Shah (D) vs. Feely (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: AZ-6 (Tucson suburbs)
why_it_matters: Ciscomani has won twice by under three points.
notes: Mendoza (D) vs. Ciscomani (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: CA-11 (San Francisco)
why_it_matters: Pelosi's retirement set up a progressive-versus-establishment fight for one of the safest Democratic seats in the country.
notes: Top two: Wiener (D) vs. Chan (D). Chakrabarti was eliminated. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: CA-13 (Central Valley: Merced, Modesto)
why_it_matters: Gray won by 187 votes in 2024. Prop 50 redrew the district to be friendlier to Democrats.
notes: Gray (D) vs. a Republican; Wikipedia is inconsistent on whether that is Kevin Lincoln or Vin Kruttiventi. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: CA-22 (Bakersfield, Kings County)
why_it_matters: Valadao voted for the Medicaid cuts in the 2025 budget bill in a district with one of the highest Medicaid shares in the country, then Prop 50 made the seat bluer.
notes: Valadao (R) vs. Villegas (D), a Medicare for All progressive. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: CA-45 (Little Saigon, north Orange County)
why_it_matters: Tran flipped this seat by 653 votes in 2024.
notes: Tran (D) vs. Vo (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: CO-8 (Adams and Weld counties)
why_it_matters: The most evenly divided district in Colorado. Evans won by under a point in 2024.
notes: Rutinel (D) vs. Evans (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: GA-13 (south metro Atlanta)
why_it_matters: Scott, 80, drew a crowded primary from younger challengers. A generational-change test in a safe seat.
notes: Jasmine Clark (D) vs. Chavez (R). David Scott left office in April and lost the primary. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: IA-1 (southeast Iowa, Davenport)
why_it_matters: Miller-Meeks survived by 799 votes in 2024. Bohannan is back for a third try.
notes: Bohannan (D) vs. Miller-Meeks (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: IL-7 (Chicago West Side, downtown)
why_it_matters: Davis retired after 15 terms. Kina Collins, who came within four points of him in 2022, ran again in a crowded field.
notes: La Shawn Ford (D) vs. Koppie (R). Kina Collins lost the primary. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: IL-9 (Chicago North Side, Evanston)
why_it_matters: Schakowsky's retirement opened a deep-blue seat. Kat Abughazaleh's small-dollar campaign against a field of state legislators drew national attention.
notes: Biss (D) vs. Elleson (R). Abughazaleh lost the primary. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: ME-2 (northern Maine)
why_it_matters: Golden retired from a Trump +9 district. Former governor Paul LePage is the Republican nominee.
notes: Dunlap (D) vs. LePage (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: MI-7 (Lansing)
why_it_matters: Open in 2024 when Slotkin left for the Senate; Barrett won by under four points.
notes: Lawrence (D) vs. Barrett (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: MI-10 (Macomb County)
why_it_matters: James left to run for governor. Democrats came within half a point here in 2022.
notes: Hines (D) vs. Bouchard (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: MI-13 (Detroit)
why_it_matters: Justice Democrats backed state Rep. Donavan McKinney against self-funding incumbent Thanedar. The marquee progressive primary challenge of the cycle.
notes: McKinney (D) beat incumbent Thanedar. Confirm the general election opponent. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: NE-2 (Omaha)
why_it_matters: Bacon retired from a Harris-won district. Best Democratic pickup chance in the Plains.
notes: Denise Powell (D) vs. Harding (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: NJ-7 (Hunterdon, Warren, western Union)
why_it_matters: Kean underperformed Trump in 2024 and Sherrill carried the district in the 2025 governor's race.
notes: Bennett (D) vs. Kean (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: NY-7 (Brooklyn, Queens)
why_it_matters: Velázquez retired from the most DSA-friendly district in the country. Claire Valdez ran with NYC-DSA backing against establishment-aligned Democrats.
notes: Claire Valdez (D) vs. Rivera (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: NY-10 (Lower Manhattan, brownstone Brooklyn)
why_it_matters: Former NYC comptroller Brad Lander challenged Goldman from the left in the highest-profile House primary in the city.
notes: Lander (D) vs. Moore (R). Goldman lost. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: NY-12 (Manhattan: Upper East and West Sides)
why_it_matters: Nadler's retirement produced a large field including Assemblymembers Micah Lasher and Alex Bores and Jack Schlossberg.
notes: Lasher (D) vs. Shinkle (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: NY-17 (Hudson Valley: Rockland, Putnam, north Westchester)
why_it_matters: Harris carried the district. Lawler is the top Democratic target in New York.
notes: Cait Conley (D) vs. Lawler (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: NC-1 (northeast North Carolina)
why_it_matters: The legislature redrew NC-1 in October 2025 specifically to unseat Davis.
notes: Davis (D) vs. Buckhout (R) in the redrawn district. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: OH-9 (Toledo)
why_it_matters: Kaptur, the longest-serving woman in Congress, holds a Trump district under a new 2026 map.
notes: Kaptur (D) vs. Merrin (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: OH-13 (Akron)
why_it_matters: Sykes won by two points in 2024 and the 2026 map shifted the district slightly right.
notes: Sykes (D) vs. Coleman (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: PA-1 (Bucks County)
why_it_matters: Harris carried the district but Fitzpatrick's crossover appeal has held for four cycles.
notes: Harvie (D) vs. Fitzpatrick (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: PA-3 (Philadelphia)
why_it_matters: Evans retired. State Sen. Sharif Street and state Rep. Chris Rabb, a Working Families-aligned progressive, led the field.
notes: Chris Rabb (D) vs. Mahoney (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: PA-7 (Lehigh Valley)
why_it_matters: Mackenzie ousted Susan Wild by one point in 2024.
notes: Bob Brooks (D) vs. Mackenzie (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: PA-8 (Scranton, Wilkes-Barre)
why_it_matters: Bresnahan beat Matt Cartwright by under two points and has drawn stock-trading scrutiny.
notes: Cognetti (D) vs. Bresnahan (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: TX-18 (Houston)
why_it_matters: Menefee won the January 2026 special. Al Green, drawn out of TX-9 by the 2025 map, challenged him for the full term.
notes: Menefee (D) vs. Whitfield (R). Green lost the runoff. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: TX-28 (Laredo, south Texas)
why_it_matters: Cuellar, under federal indictment and one of the most conservative House Democrats, is running in a redrawn seat.
notes: Cuellar (D) vs. Tijerina (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: TX-34 (Rio Grande Valley)
why_it_matters: The 2025 map made this Valley seat significantly redder.
notes: Gonzalez (D) vs. Eric Flores (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: TX-37 (Austin)
why_it_matters: Doggett stepped aside after the 2025 map carved up Greg Casar's TX-35. Casar, chair of the Progressive Caucus, is running here.
notes: Casar (D) vs. Peña (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: UT-1 (Salt Lake County, court-ordered map)
why_it_matters: A state court ordered a map with a Democratic-leaning Salt Lake City seat for 2026, the first realistic Democratic House seat in Utah in a decade.
notes: McAdams (D) vs. Owen (R). Blake Moore moved to the 2nd district. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: WI-3 (western Wisconsin, La Crosse, Eau Claire)
why_it_matters: Rebecca Cooke came within three points in 2024 and is running again.
notes: Cooke (D) vs. Van Orden (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Texas Senate
why_it_matters: A Cornyn-Paxton Republican runoff and a Talarico-Crockett Democratic primary made this the most expensive Senate race in the country.
notes: Talarico (D) vs. Paxton (R). Cornyn lost the runoff. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Michigan Senate
why_it_matters: Abdul El-Sayed ran an explicitly progressive campaign against Rep. Haley Stevens and state Sen. Mallory McMorrow. The Republican is Mike Rogers.
notes: El-Sayed (D) vs. Rogers (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Minnesota Senate
why_it_matters: Lt. Gov. Peggy Flanagan (progressive) vs. Rep. Angie Craig (moderate) for an open seat.
notes: Flanagan (D) vs. Tafoya (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Maine Senate
why_it_matters: Oysterman and veteran Graham Platner's insurgent campaign against Gov. Janet Mills for the right to face Collins.
notes: Troy Jackson (D, chosen by convention) vs. Collins (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: North Carolina Senate
why_it_matters: Former governor Roy Cooper against former RNC chair Michael Whatley. The Democrats' best pickup opportunity.
notes: Cooper (D) vs. Whatley (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Georgia Senate
why_it_matters: The most vulnerable Democratic incumbent.
notes: Ossoff (D) vs. Mike Collins (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Ohio Senate (special)
why_it_matters: Sherrod Brown's comeback bid for the seat J.D. Vance vacated.
notes: Brown (D) vs. Husted (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Iowa Senate
why_it_matters: Ernst retired. Rep. Ashley Hinson is the Republican; Democrats ran a four-way primary.
notes: Turek (D) vs. Hinson (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Illinois Senate
why_it_matters: Lt. Gov. Juliana Stratton vs. Reps. Raja Krishnamoorthi and Robin Kelly for Durbin's seat, decided in the March primary.
notes: Stratton (D) vs. Tracy (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: New Hampshire Senate
why_it_matters: Rep. Chris Pappas against former Sen. John E. Sununu.
notes: Republican primary is Sept 8, 2026: Sununu vs. Brown. Pappas is the presumptive Democratic nominee. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Massachusetts Senate
why_it_matters: Rep. Seth Moulton challenged the 80-year-old Green New Deal co-author from the center.
notes: Markey (D) vs. Deaton (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Nebraska Senate
why_it_matters: Independent union leader Dan Osborn, who came within seven points of Deb Fischer in 2024, is running again with no Democrat on the ballot.

title: California Governor
why_it_matters: A sprawling top-two field. Whether two Democrats or a Democrat and a Republican advanced decides how progressive the general election can be.
notes: Top two: Becerra (D) vs. Hilton (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: New York Governor
why_it_matters: Lt. Gov. Antonio Delgado primaried Hochul. Republican Bruce Blakeman is the nominee after Elise Stefanik withdrew.
notes: Hochul (D) vs. Blakeman (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Michigan Governor
why_it_matters: A three-way general: Democrat Jocelyn Benson, Detroit mayor Mike Duggan as an independent, and a Republican.
notes: Benson (D) vs. James (R), with Duggan running as an independent. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Wisconsin Governor
why_it_matters: Evers retired. A crowded Democratic primary with a clear progressive lane (Francesca Hong, Mandela Barnes) versus establishment candidates.
notes: Crowley (D) vs. Tiffany (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Georgia Governor
why_it_matters: Former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms led the Democratic field; Trump-endorsed Lt. Gov. Burt Jones led the Republicans.
notes: Bottoms (D) vs. Rick Jackson (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Arizona Governor
why_it_matters: Hobbs is the most vulnerable Democratic governor. Rep. Andy Biggs and Karrin Taylor Robson fought for the Republican nomination.
notes: Hobbs (D) vs. Biggs (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Ohio Governor
why_it_matters: Former state health director Amy Acton against Vivek Ramaswamy.
notes: Acton (D) vs. Ramaswamy (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Florida Governor
why_it_matters: Former Republican congressman David Jolly is the Democrat against Trump-endorsed Rep. Byron Donalds.
notes: Jolly (D) vs. Donalds (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Iowa Governor
why_it_matters: State Auditor Rob Sand, the only Democrat holding statewide office, raised record sums for an open seat.
notes: Sand (D) vs. Lahn (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Nevada Governor
why_it_matters: Attorney General Aaron Ford is the Democrat against Lombardo in a state Trump carried in 2024.
notes: Ford (D) vs. Lombardo (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Maine Governor
why_it_matters: Former Senate President Troy Jackson, a logger and Sanders-aligned populist, ran against Hannah Pingree, Shenna Bellows, and Angus King III.
notes: Pingree (D) vs. Charles (R) vs. Bennett (I). Troy Jackson moved to the Senate race. Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.

title: Minnesota Governor
why_it_matters: Walz ended his campaign in January 2026; Sen. Amy Klobuchar entered the race for the open seat.
notes: Klobuchar (D) vs. Demuth (R). Per Wikipedia, checked Sept 2, 2026.
